items.title: Smooth developments of constrained initial data, data-fixing isometries, development embeddings and maximality
items.statement:
**Data.** Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, a smooth three-manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary, a smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $K$. The normal convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Specify one fixed covariant matter model, consisting of a finite list of smooth tensor fields $\psi$, fixed equations $\mathcal E(g,\psi)=0$ and a fixed stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\psi)$, with pullback by local diffeomorphisms commuting with the equations and stress. Fix its complete smooth Cauchy data $d$: these determine all independent matter initial variables, not only the normal stress projections. Initial tensors with normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb R\nu\oplus T\Sigma$ with metric $g_0(a\nu+X,b\nu+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. In a development, identify $a\nu+X$ with $an+dj(X)$.

An admissible fixed coupled model is one satisfying the complete initialization, hyperbolic reduction, recovery and comparison hypotheses of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]], or a specified independent local existence and uniqueness reduction such as the dust branch below. The same fixed model, complete data and admissibility conditions are used in every comparison and at every restart. Admissibility includes the applicability of its supplied complete-data local existence and geometric uniqueness theorem to the data realized on each spacelike restart surface of the compared solutions. This must be checked for the actual model and surface; it is not inferred from stress conservation. This class includes the following four concrete branches; they do not exhaust it.

1. **Vacuum:** no matter fields, $\mathcal T=0$, and empty matter data.
2. **Scalar field:** fix one smooth potential $V$ and one normalization $K_\phi>0$. The field is $\varphi$, its equation is $\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$, its stress is the expression in [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] clause (c), and its complete data are $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ with $\pi_0=n(\varphi)|_\Sigma$. The fixed potential has no sign restriction ([[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]]).
3. **Strict barotropic fluid:** fix a smooth EOS $P:J\to\mathbb R$ on an open interval with $\epsilon+P(\epsilon)>0$ and $0<P'(\epsilon)<1$. The fields are $\epsilon\in J$ and future unit velocity $u$, the stress is $(\epsilon+P(\epsilon))u^\flat\otimes u^\flat+P(\epsilon)g$, and the equations are the continuity and Euler equations of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] clause (c), with this fixed EOS. Complete data are $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$, where $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, equivalently the bundle velocity $U_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}(\nu+v_0)$. No small-tilt restriction is imposed ([[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]]).
4. **Geodesic nonnegative dust:** the fields are an energy-coefficient density $\varepsilon\ge0$ and a smooth future unit timelike field $u$, including on $\{\varepsilon=0\}$. Set $\mathcal T=\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$ and require both $\nabla_u u=0$ and $u(\varepsilon)+\varepsilon\nabla_a u^a=0$ everywhere. Complete data are $(\varepsilon_0,U_0)$, with $\varepsilon_0\ge0$ and prescribed smooth future unit bundle velocity $U_0$, equivalently arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt. On positive-density regions this is [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]] with its density parameter equal to $\varepsilon$. Through empty regions the geodesic velocity is separately prescribed and matched; conservation of stress alone is not substituted for this full system. For a fixed $c>0$, the mass-normalized theorem [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] applies with $\rho_0=\varepsilon_0/c^2$ and reconstructs $\varepsilon=c^2\rho$.

Require the constraints for the initial stress $T_0$ computed from this complete data on $\mathcal V$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(\nu,\nu),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(\nu,\cdot).$$
These use the convention of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]. Equality of data includes equality of the model, constants, potential or EOS, and every component of $d$.

The local Cauchy-development and uniqueness suppliers for vacuum, scalar and strict fluid are the fixed-model theorem [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] and the two concrete branch theorems above. Its harmonic route requires the same fixed extraction/reconstruction rules and smooth symmetric-hyperbolic coefficient family for every compared physical solution, a positive time matrix on an admissible open state set, complete compatible initialization from $(h,K,d)$, propagation of auxiliary compatibility with recovery of the full matter equations on the reduced solution, and stress conservation on that reduced solution before Einstein recovery. These are the three explicit hypotheses of that theorem; conservation alone does not supply a Cauchy evolution law. Dust uses its independent common-flow/parallel-frame initialization, hyperbolic reduction, subsidiary recovery and uniqueness of [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]], rather than being asserted to satisfy the harmonic metric-first-derivative matter contract. Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are carried wherever these local theorems are invoked. Every additional fixed coupled model must supply the same complete-data local existence, admissibility, recovery and uniqueness obligations before it is used. This definition makes no local or global existence assertion.

**(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. the smooth tensor fields $\psi$ of the fixed model over $M$;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $E(g,\psi)=0$;
5. the initial condition on $j(\Sigma)$: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of
   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one
   parameter value;
6. the induced data: $j^*(g)=h$, the second fundamental form of $j$ with
   respect to the future unit normal equals $K$ in the convention
   $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ of
   [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], and
   the initial data of $\psi$ on $j(\Sigma)$ transported by $j$ equal $d$.

No completeness of $(M,g)$, no inextendibility of $M$, and no claim that the
equations hold beyond $M$ are part of the definition. Whether a development is
globally hyperbolic is not part of the definition either; by clause 5 it
follows from [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(b) Data-fixing isometry.** A **data-fixing isometry** between developments
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data is a smooth
diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ such that

1. $\varphi^*(g')=g$;
2. $g'_{\varphi(p)}(d\varphi_pN_p,N'_{\varphi(p)})<0$ for every $p\in M$: the isometry carries the future cone of $N$ onto that of $N'$;
3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, with the natural pullback action on every listed tensor type (and the inverse differential on contravariant slots). Equality includes every listed field, including the prescribed dust velocity at zero density.

**(c) Development embedding.** A **development embedding** of $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$
into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**(d) Maximality.** A development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the given data is
**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

**(e) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition of the solution class used by
the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,d)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

items.title: Common subdevelopments, maximal common developments and corresponding boundary points
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be two developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]].

**(a) Common subdevelopment.** A **common subdevelopment** of $M$ and $M'$ is
a pair $(U,\varphi)$ in which

1. $U\subseteq M$ is an open subset with $j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$ such that the
   restriction $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ is a development of the same data
   (with the induced field equations on the open submanifold $U$); and
2. $\varphi:(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)\to(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a development
   embedding in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]
   clause (c).

Here "the induced field equations on $U$" means the equations of clause (a)4
of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] restricted to $U$; the
induced Lorentzian manifold is $(U,g|_U)$ with the time orientation $N|_U$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(b) Maximal common development.** A common subdevelopment $(U^*,\varphi^*)$
is a **maximal common development** (MCD) of $M$ and $M'$ when for every
common subdevelopment $(U,\varphi)$ one has $U\subseteq U^*$ and
$\varphi^*|_U=\varphi$. Existence is not asserted by this definition; it is
proved in [[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]].

**(c) Corresponding boundary points.** Let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common
subdevelopment. Its **corresponding boundary points** are pairs
$(p,p')\in\partial^M U\times\partial^{M'}\varphi(U)$, where the boundaries are
taken in $M$ and in $M'$ respectively, such that for every open neighbourhood
$V$ of $p$ in $M$ and every open neighbourhood $V'$ of $p'$ in $M'$ there is
$x\in V\cap U$ with $\varphi(x)\in V'$.

**(d) Side of the initial surface.** For a corresponding pair $(p,p')$: if
$V,V'$ range over a base of neighbourhoods, the condition of (c) forces every
$x$ witnessing it to lie on one side of $j(\Sigma)$: either $x\in I^+(j(\Sigma))$
for cofinally many witnesses, or $x\in I^-(j(\Sigma))$ for cofinally many
witnesses, but not both, since $I^\pm(j(\Sigma))$ are open and determined by
the trichotomy of [[lem-gr-cauchy-set-topology-and-graph]]. The corresponding
pair is then said to lie to the **future** or to the **past** of the initial
surface; the future case is the one used in this batch, the past case being
its time reverse.

**(e) Scope.** These are mathematical relations between two fixed developments
and their boundary points. Neither the existence of boundary points, nor the
existence of a common subdevelopment with nonempty boundary, nor uniqueness of
a corresponding point, is asserted here.

items.title: A development sharing the initial Cauchy surface with a larger development is causally convex in it
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ be as in
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a): $M$ is
a development of the given data, $U\subseteq M$ is open with
$j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$, and $U$ with the restricted fields is again a
development of the same data. Write $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and compute
$I^\pm$, $J^\pm$ and $\le$ in $M$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). Then:

**(a) Past convexity within the future of $\Sigma$.** For every future causal
curve $\nu:[a,b]\to M$ with $\nu(a)\in\Sigma$ and $\nu(b)\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$
one has $\nu([a,b])\subseteq U$.

**(b) Future convexity within the past of $\Sigma$.** For every future causal
curve $\nu:[a,b]\to M$ with $\nu(a)\in U\cap I^-(\Sigma)$ and
$\nu(b)\in\Sigma$ one has $\nu([a,b])\subseteq U$.

**(c) Segments with endpoints in $U$.** For every future causal curve
$\nu:[a,b]\to M$ with $\nu(a),\nu(b)\in U$ one has $\nu([a,b])\subseteq U$.

items.title: A maximal connected portion of an inextendible causal curve inside an open subset is inextendible there
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $V\subseteq U\subseteq M$ be open
subsets with the induced metric and time orientation, and let
$\gamma:I\to U$ be a future causal curve
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) that is inextendible in the
Lorentzian manifold $U$: $\gamma$ does not converge to any point of $U$ as its
parameter tends to either end of $I$ (clause (d) of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], read with ambient set $U$). Let $J$
be a connected component of
$$\gamma^{-1}[V]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in V\}.$$
Then $\gamma|_J$, regarded as a future causal curve in the Lorentzian manifold
$V$ with the restricted fields, is inextendible in $V$.

items.title: Rigidity of isometric immersions of a connected Lorentzian manifold, and agreement of data-fixing embeddings on overlaps
items.statement:
Throughout, for a smooth map $\psi:N\to N'$ between smooth Lorentzian
four-manifolds write $\psi^*(g')=g$ when $g_p(v,w)=g'_{\psi(p)}(d\psi_pv,d\psi_pw)$
for all $p\in N$ and $v,w\in T_pN$; such a map is an **isometric immersion**
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). Let $\nabla,\nabla'$ be
the metric-selected connections ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let geodesics
and exponential maps be those of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]].

**(a) Rigidity.** Let $N$ be connected and let
$\psi_1,\psi_2:N\to N'$ be isometric immersions with
$\psi_1(p)=\psi_2(p)$ and $d\psi_1(p)=d\psi_2(p)$ for some $p\in N$. Then
$\psi_1=\psi_2$, that is, $\psi_1(q)=\psi_2(q)$ and $d\psi_1(q)=d\psi_2(q)$
for every $q\in N$.

**(b) Data-fixing embeddings have equal differentials on the initial surface.**
Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$, $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ and $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ be
as in [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a),
and let $\psi_1,\psi_2:U\to M'$ be development embeddings in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c). Then
$d\psi_1=d\psi_2$ at every point of $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$.

**(c) Agreement on overlaps.** Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$
be developments of the same data, and let $(U_1,\psi_1)$ and $(U_2,\psi_2)$ be
common subdevelopments in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Then
$\psi_1=\psi_2$ on $U_1\cap U_2$.

items.title: A data-fixing isometric immersion of developments is injective, hence a development embedding; uniqueness of data-fixing embeddings
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause
(a), with $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$ and $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$. Let
$\varphi:M\to M'$ be a smooth map with $\varphi^*(g')=g$, with
$g'_{\varphi(p)}(d\varphi_pN_p,N'_{\varphi(p)})<0$ for every $p\in M$, with
$\varphi\circ j=j'$ and $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$ (so $\varphi$ is a future isometric immersion fixing the complete data and matching every matter field).
Then:

**(a)** $d\varphi_p:T_pM\to T_{\varphi(p)}M'$ is an isomorphism for every
$p\in M$;

**(b)** $\varphi$ is injective, hence a diffeomorphism onto the open subset
$\varphi(M)\subseteq M'$ and therefore a development embedding in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c);

**(c)** if $M$ is connected and $\psi_1,\psi_2:M\to M'$ are two such
data-fixing isometric immersions, then $\psi_1=\psi_2$; in particular every
data-fixing self-isometry of a connected development is the identity of $M$.

Sbierski, On the Existence of a Maximal Cauchy Development for the Einstein Equations - a Dezornification, arXiv:1309.7591v3 (2015): Lemma 3.3 with proof (an isometric immersion whose restriction to the Cauchy surface is a diffeomorphism is an isometric embedding) and the remark following it, printed pp. 13-14
E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: maximal geodesics and the exponential map, Theorems 2.4-2.6 printed pp. 26-27

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the maximal common development of two developments
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data
in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a),
with $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$. Then there exist $U^*\subseteq M$ and
$\psi^*:U^*\to M'$ such that:

**(a)** $(U^*,\psi^*)$ is a common subdevelopment of $M$ and $M'$ in the sense
of [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a);

**(b)** for every common subdevelopment $(U,\varphi)$ of $M$ and $M'$ one has
$U\subseteq U^*$ and $\psi^*|_U=\varphi$; in particular $(U^*,\psi^*)$ is a
maximal common development in the sense of clause (b) of that definition, and
it contains $j(\Sigma)$;

**(c)** uniqueness: if $(U^\dagger,\psi^\dagger)$ also satisfies (a) and (b),
then $U^\dagger=U^*$ and $\psi^\dagger=\psi^*$.

references.title: J. Sbierski, On the Existence of a Maximal Cauchy Development for the Einstein Equations - a Dezornification, arXiv:1309.7591v3 (2015): Theorem 3.4 with proof (the union of all common globally hyperbolic developments is the maximal common development), printed p. 14
P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): Cauchy hypersurfaces, domains of dependence and global hyperbolicity of domains, Theorem 2.9.9 printed pp. 46-50

items.title: Structure of corresponding boundary points: achronality of the future boundary, equality of pasts, and uniqueness
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]).

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$, $I^\pm=I^\pm_M$ and
$I'^\pm=I^\pm_{M'}$. Then:

**(a)** $\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ is achronal in $M$, and
$\partial\varphi(U)\cap I'^+(\Sigma')$ is achronal in $M'$.

**(b)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding
boundary points to the future of the initial surface. Then
$$\varphi\bigl(I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U),$$
and for every $q\in I^-(p)\cap U$ also
$$\varphi\bigl(I^+(q)\cap I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^+(\varphi(q))\cap I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U).$$

**(c)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding.
If $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,0)\to U$ is a future timelike curve with
$\gamma(s)\to p$ as $s\nearrow0$, then $\varphi(\gamma(s))\to p'$ as
$s\nearrow0$. Moreover $p$ has at most one corresponding boundary point.

items.title: The set of boundary points with a corresponding point is open, and the extension preserves the metric, matter fields and connection on the closure side
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]).

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Let
$$C:=\{p\in\partial U:\ p\text{ has a corresponding boundary point in }\partial\varphi(U)\}$$
be the set of boundary points of $U$ that have a corresponding point (clause
(c) of that definition). Then:

**(a)** $C$ is open in $\partial U$: there is an open set $G\subseteq M$ with
$C=G\cap\partial U$.

**(b)** There is an open set $\Omega\subseteq M$ with $U\cup C\subseteq\Omega$
and a smooth map $\Phi:\Omega\to M'$ whose restriction to $U$ is $\varphi$ and
whose value at $p\in C$ is the unique corresponding boundary point of $p$;
moreover, for every $p\in C$ there is an open neighbourhood
$W_p\subseteq\Omega$ of $p$ and a smooth **local diffeomorphism**
$$\widehat\varphi_p:W_p\to M',\qquad \widehat\varphi_p(q)=\exp_{\varphi(a_p)}\bigl(d\varphi_{a_p}(\exp_{a_p}^{-1}q)\bigr)$$
built from a common interior base point $a_p\in U$, chosen in $I^-(p)$ when $p$ is to the future of the initial surface and in $I^+(p)$ when $p$ is to its past, and the
exponential maps, such that $\widehat\varphi_p=\varphi$ on $W_p\cap U$ and
$\Phi=\widehat\varphi_p$ on $W_p\cap(U\cup C)$. No isometry property of
$\widehat\varphi_p$ on the part of $W_p$ outside $\overline U$ is claimed.

**(c)** At every point $q\in U\cup C$ the map $\Phi$ preserves the metric, the
matter fields and the metric-selected connection:

1. $g'_{\Phi(q)}(d\Phi_qv,d\Phi_qw)=g_q(v,w)$ for all $v,w\in T_qM$, so
   $\Phi^*(g')=g$ on $U\cup C$;
2. $(\Phi^*\psi'^i)_q=\psi^i_q$ for every listed matter field $i$;
3. for all smooth vector fields $X,Y$ defined on a neighbourhood of $q$ and
   every $q\in U\cup C$,
   $$\nabla'_{d\Phi\,X}d\Phi\,Y=d\Phi\bigl(\nabla_XY\bigr)\quad\text{at }\Phi(q),$$
   equivalently the pullback connection $\Phi^*\nabla'$ equals $\nabla$ at
   $q$, where both sides are read through the invertible differential
   $d\Phi_q$.

**(d)** Every geodesic segment of $(M,g)$ whose image is contained in $U\cup C$
is mapped by $\Phi$ to a geodesic segment of $(M',g')$; a null geodesic
segment is mapped to a null geodesic segment.

**(e)** Let $S\subseteq U\cup C$ be an embedded submanifold of $M$. Then
$\Phi|_S$ is an injective immersion, hence an embedding onto its image, and it
carries the induced metric of $S$, its second fundamental form with respect to
any unit normal field, and the matter fields together with their covariant derivatives of every finite order along $S$ to the corresponding objects of $\Phi(S)$ in
$M'$. In particular $(S,\bar g_S,k_S,\psi|_S)$ and
$(\Phi(S),\bar g_{\Phi(S)},k_{\Phi(S)},\psi'|_{\Phi(S)})$ are identified by

items.title: Affine extension of geodesics confined to a compact set with finite auxiliary length, and the logarithmic speed bound
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let geodesics
be the maximal geodesics with their affine parametrizations supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Let $h$ be a smooth
positive definite metric on $M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]).

**(a)** For every compact $K\subseteq M$ there is a constant $c(K)\in[0,\infty)$
with the following property. Let $\gamma:J\to M$ be a nonconstant geodesic,
let $q>0$ be the $h$-speed of its affine velocity and let $\ell$ denote the
$h$-arclength parameter of $\gamma$, so that $q(\ell):=|d\gamma/d\lambda|_h$
is the $h$-norm of the affine velocity expressed in the parameter $\ell$. At
every parameter value with $\gamma(\ell)\in K$ one has
$$\left|\frac{d\log q}{d\ell}\right|\le c(K).$$

**(b)** Assume in addition that $(M,d_h)$ is complete and that every closed
$d_h$-bounded subset of $M$ is compact. Let $\gamma:(\alpha,\beta)\to M$ be a
maximal nonconstant geodesic with $\beta<+\infty$, let $\lambda_0\in(\alpha,\beta)$,
and let $K\subseteq M$ be compact with $\gamma([\lambda_0,\beta))\subseteq K$.
Suppose that the $h$-arclength of the tail is finite:
$$\int_{\lambda_0}^{\beta}\bigl|\gamma'(\lambda)\bigr|_h\,d\lambda<\infty .$$
Then the geodesic extends beyond $\beta$, contradicting the maximality of
$(\alpha,\beta)$; consequently no maximal geodesic can have a finite affine
endpoint while its tail remains in a compact set and has finite
$h$-arclength.

items.title: Time separation in a globally hyperbolic manifold: finiteness, existence of maximizing geodesics and the radial formula on causally convex normal regions
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), let
$L_g$ be the Lorentzian length functional on future causal curves
([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), and for $q\in M$ define the
**time separation**
$$\tau_q:M\to[0,\infty),\qquad \tau_q(r):=\sup\{L_g(\alpha):\ \alpha \text{ is a future causal curve from } r \text{ to } q\},$$
the supremum over the empty set being $0$; thus $\tau_q(r)>0$ exactly for
$r\in I^-(q)$ and $\tau_q(r)=0$ for $r\notin J^-(q)$.

**(a)** For every $r\in J^-(q)$ one has $0\le\tau_q(r)<\infty$. If $r\ne q$, the supremum is attained by a future causal curve $\gamma$ from $r$ to $q$ with $L_g(\gamma)=\tau_q(r)$. Every such **nondegenerate maximizer** is, up to increasing reparametrization, a causal geodesic, with image in the compact set $J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$. For $r=q$, $\tau_q(q)=0$ and the constant zero-velocity geodesic is the **degenerate maximizer** by convention. It has image $\{q\}$ and length zero; it is not asserted to belong to the curve class requiring nonzero causal velocity almost everywhere. This separates the reflexive case without changing the separation function or the nondegenerate maximizing claim.

**(b)** Let $V$ be a strictly convex normal neighbourhood of $q$ (as produced
by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and let $W\subseteq V$ be open and
causally convex in $M$ (every causal curve in $M$ with both endpoints in $W$
is contained in $W$), with $\overline W$ compact and $q\in W$. Then for every
$r\in W\cap I^-(q)$,
$$\tau_q(r)=\sqrt{-g_q\bigl(\exp_q^{-1}(r),\exp_q^{-1}(r)\bigr)},$$
so $\tau_q$ is smooth on $W\cap I^-(q)$ and extends continuously by
$\tau_q(q)=0$ and $\tau_q(r)=0$ for $r\in W\setminus J^-(q)$.

**(c)** On every compact set $K\subseteq M$ the function $\tau_q$ is upper
semicontinuous in the following strong form: for every sequence $r_n\to r$ in
$K$ one has $\limsup_n\tau_q(r_n)\le\tau_q(r)$. If moreover $r\in I^-(q)$,
then $\tau_q(r_n)\to\tau_q(r)$ for every sequence $r_n\to r$.

items.title: The spacelike restart surface at an exposed boundary point: maximizers on the boundary, the level hypersurface and its radial tube
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data
([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]), $(U,\varphi)$ a common
subdevelopment ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]
clause (a)), $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $p\in\partial U$ be an exposed
boundary point in the sense of [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]]:
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$
Fix a strictly convex normal neighbourhood $C$ of $p$
([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) with $C\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$ and
$C\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, where $C_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the
corresponding set of [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] (possible
because that set is open in $\partial U$ and $I^+(\Sigma)$ is open). Let
$p_1\ll p\ll p_2$ be points of $C$ such that $W:=I^+(p_1)\cap I^-(p_2)$
satisfies $\overline W\subseteq C$ (possible: strong causality at $p$ supplies
a neighbourhood $V_2\subseteq C$ of $p$ such that every causal curve with
both endpoints in $V_2$ is contained in $C$, and then
$\overline W\subseteq J^+(p_1)\cap J^-(p_2)\subseteq C$ for $p_1,p_2\in V_2$
by the same argument). Then $W$ is open, causally convex, $p\in W$, and
$\overline W$ is compact. Let $q\in W\cap I^+(p)$ be a point with
$$J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W,$$
chosen so close to $p$ along a future timelike curve that also $q\in W$
([[lem-gr-exposed-boundary-point]]). Let $\tau_q$ be the time separation from
$q$ ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]]) and put
$$K:=\overline W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma),\qquad \tau_0:=\max\{\tau_q(r):r\in K\}.$$
Let $W^\circ:=W\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and let $S$ be the connected component of
the closed-in-$W^\circ$ set $\{x\in W^\circ:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ that contains
a maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$. Then:

**(a)** $\tau_0>0$; every maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$ lies in
$W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$; every $x\in W$ with
$\tau_q(x)>\tau_0$ lies in $U$; every $x\in W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with
$\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$ lies in $\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(b)** $S$ is a nonempty smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface of $M$
without boundary, subsets $S\subseteq(W\cap U)\cup(W\cap\partial U\cap
C_{\mathrm{corr}})$ and $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$; moreover
$S\subseteq\{x:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ and every point of $S\cap U^c$ lies in
$\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(c)** There is a smooth positive function $\delta:S\to(0,\infty)$ with the
following properties. Define $X:=\nabla\tau_q/g(\nabla\tau_q,\nabla\tau_q)$
(so that $d\tau_q(X)=1$) on $\{\tau_q>0\}\cap W$, let $\phi_t$ be its local
flow, and put
$$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to M,\qquad F(s,t):=\phi_t(s),\qquad N:=F\bigl(S\times(-\delta,\delta)\bigr).$$
Then $F$ is well defined and smooth, $N\subseteq W$ is open,
$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to N$ is a diffeomorphism,
$\tau_q(F(s,t))=\tau_0+t$, and:

1. every causal curve in $N$ is, in the coordinates $(s,t)$, of the form
   $t\mapsto F(s(t),t)$ with $s(t)$ of finite length in the induced metric
   of $S$, and it meets $S$ in at most one parameter value;
2. every causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$ meets
   $U$, and consequently meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; in
   particular no causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$
   and whose image is disjoint from $U$ exists;
3. for every $y\in N\cap U$ there is a unique $s\in S$ with $y=F(s,t_y)$, and the **punctured radial segment**
$$\{F(s,u):u\text{ between }0\text{ and }t_y,\ u\ne0\}$$
is contained in $U$. The base belongs to $U\cup C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, and the full segment including the base is contained in $U$ whenever $s\in U$. In particular, if $t_y<0$ then also $s\in U$. If $\Theta:N\to M'$ is a time-orientation-preserving local isometry with $\Theta|_S=\Phi|_S$, where $\Phi$ is the smooth extension of the common-subdevelopment map $\varphi$, then $\Theta=\varphi$ on $N\cap U$;
4. the tube can be chosen inside any prescribed open neighbourhood $O\subseteq W$ of the whole $S$, and below any prescribed positive continuous width ceiling on $S$. More quantitatively, write $q_0=g|_{TS}$ and $q_t=F_t^*g|_{TS}$. The construction gives $0<\delta<\tau_0/8$, $q_t\ge\tfrac12q_0$ for $|t|<\delta(s)$ and $|d\delta|_{q_0}\le1/(8\sqrt2)$. Every smooth positive smaller width $\widetilde\delta\le\delta$ satisfying $|d\widetilde\delta|_{q_0}\le1/(4\sqrt2)$ retains conclusions 1-3.

No compactness of $S$ or positive uniform lower bound for $\delta$ is assumed. The radial segment in clause 3 excludes its base because $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$.

items.title: The causal domain of dependence of a partial Cauchy hypersurface is an open causally convex manifold on which the hypersurface is Cauchy
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(W,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let $S\subseteq W$ be a closed acausal edgeless embedded topological hypersurface of codimension one. Here acausality forbids causal relations between distinct points of $S$ as in [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]; **edgeless** means that no $s\in S$ has the following property: every open neighborhood $U$ of $s$ admits $a\in I^-_U(s)$, $b\in I^+_U(s)$ and a timelike curve in $U$ from $a$ to $b$ avoiding $S$. All curves and inextendibility use [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], so an inextendible end has no point limit in the specified ambient manifold. Define the ambient causal domains by
$$D^+(S)=\{p\in W:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve in }W\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\},$$
$$D^-(S)=\{p\in W:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve in }W\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\},\qquad D(S)=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S),$$
as in [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]. Then:

**(a)** $D(S)$ is open, contains $S$, and $D^\pm(S)\setminus S\subseteq I^\pm(S)$.

**(b)** Every causal curve in $W$ with endpoints in $D(S)$ lies in $D(S)$.

**(c)** Every causal curve in the induced open submanifold $D(S)$ which is inextendible there meets $S$ at exactly one parameter value. No smoothness or spacelikeness of the topological hypersurface is required.

items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice

$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data,

([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a)),
write $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $C\subseteq\partial U$ be the set of

is maximal among the common subdevelopments of $M$ and $M'$ in the following

$V\subseteq U$ and $\chi=\varphi$ on $V$ (this is the maximality property of
the maximal common development, [[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]] clause

items.title: Gluing two developments along their maximal common development: the quotient is a development containing both
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the actual maximal-common/no-boundary suppliers and the countable atlas/partition constructions. Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a)), write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$ and $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$, and let $(U,\varphi)$ be their
maximal common development
([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (b),
[[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]]). Let
$Z:=(M\sqcup M',\tau)$ be the topological disjoint union with canonical
inclusions $\iota_M:M\to Z$, $\iota_{M'}:M'\to Z$, and define a relation $\sim$ on
$Z$ by: $z\sim w$ when $z=w$, or $z=\iota_M(p)$ and $w=\iota_{M'}(\varphi(p))$ for
some $p\in U$, or $z=\iota_{M'}(p)$ and $w=\iota_M(\varphi^{-1}(p))$ for some
$p\in\varphi(U)$. Let $Q:=Z/{\sim}$ with quotient map $\pi:Z\to Q$ and
quotient topology ([[def-quotient-topology]]). Then:

**(a)** $\sim$ is an equivalence relation; $\pi\circ\iota_M:M\to Q$ and
$\pi\circ\iota_{M'}:M'\to Q$ are injective, continuous and open, hence
homeomorphisms onto the open subsets $(\pi\circ\iota_M)(M)$ and
$(\pi\circ\iota_{M'})(M')$, which cover $Q$;
$(\pi\circ\iota_M)(U)=(\pi\circ\iota_{M'})(\varphi(U))=(\pi\circ\iota_M)(M)\cap(\pi\circ\iota_{M'})(M')$;
and $Q$ is Hausdorff.

**(b)** $Q$ carries a unique structure of a second countable smooth
four-manifold ([[def-smooth-manifold]]) making $\pi\circ\iota_M$ and
$\pi\circ\iota_{M'}$ diffeomorphisms onto open subsets; a unique smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$ and matter fields $\bar\psi$ making both maps isometries preserving all matter fields. Their future cones determine a unique future-cone orientation on $Q$. There exists a smooth future timelike representative $\bar N$ of those cones, making both maps time-orientation preserving; this auxiliary vector field is not unique. These satisfy the field equations of the data on $Q$, and
$\bar j:=\pi\circ\iota_M\circ j$ is an embedding of $\Sigma$ with induced data
$(h,K,\psi_0)$, so $(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ is a development of the
data; moreover every causal curve in $Q$ that is inextendible in $Q$ meets
$\bar j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one parameter value.

**(c)** $\Psi:=\pi\circ\iota_M$ and $\Psi':=\pi\circ\iota_{M'}$ are data-fixing
development embeddings of $M$ and $M'$ into $Q$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c).

items.title: Existence of a universal development: the quotient of the set-sized family of canonical developments along pairwise maximal common developments
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix the data of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]: a smooth three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$,
one fixed admissible covariant matter model with its complete smooth Cauchy
data $d$, and constants $\Lambda,\kappa$. The model and its complete data,
including all required initial derivatives and prescribed fields on empty
regions, are fixed throughout. Assume the supplied complete-data local
existence and geometric uniqueness hypotheses apply on every spacelike
restart surface occurring in comparisons, as required by that definition.
Assume that at least one development of these data exists.
Write $Z_0:=\Sigma\times\mathbb R$ and let $j_0:\Sigma\to Z_0$,
$j_0(x):=(x,0)$.

**(a) The set-sized family.** Let $\mathcal X$ be the collection of all
tuples $(U,g,N,\psi)$ such that $U\subseteq Z_0$ is an open neighbourhood of
$j_0(\Sigma)$ in $Z_0$, $g$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $U$, $N$ a time
orientation and $\psi$ matter fields of the sector on $U$, and
$(U,g,N,j_0,\psi)$ is a development of the data in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a). Then
$\mathcal X$ is a set, and it is nonempty provided at least one development
of the data exists.

**(b) Identifications.** For $\alpha=(U_\alpha,g_\alpha,N_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)$
and $\beta\in\mathcal X$ let $(U_{\alpha\beta},\varphi_{\alpha\beta})$ be
their maximal common development, regarded as a subset of $U_\alpha$
([[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]], [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]];
in the convention of the definition it is realised inside the first member).
Let $Z:=\bigsqcup_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}U_\alpha$ and let $\sim$ be the
equivalence relation on $Z$ **generated** by the relations
$x\sim\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(x)$ for $\alpha,\beta\in\mathcal X$ and
$x\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ (a finite chain of such steps, in either order).
Then the classes of two points $p\in U_\alpha$, $q\in U_\beta$ coincide if and
only if $p\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ and $q=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(p)$.

**(c) The quotient.** Let $Q:=Z/{\sim}$ with quotient map $\pi$. Then
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset
$Q_\alpha:=\pi(U_\alpha)$, the family $\{Q_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}$
covers $Q$, and $Q$ is Hausdorff.

**(d) Structure.** $Q$ is a Hausdorff, second countable smooth four-manifold and carries a
unique smooth atlas (unique in the sense of maximal atlases compatible with
the charts below) making all maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms onto open
subsets, together with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, a time orientation
$\bar N$ and matter fields $\bar\psi$ such that every $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ is an
isometry onto its image preserving time orientation and matter fields, and
such that $\bar j:=\pi|_{U_\alpha}\circ j_0$ (independent of $\alpha$) is a
common embedding of $\Sigma$ with induced data $(h,K,d)$. The field
equations hold on $Q$, and every causal curve in $Q$ that is inextendible in
$Q$ meets $\bar j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one parameter value. Consequently
$(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ is a development of the data
in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a).
The representative $\bar N$ is chosen to determine the common future cones;
it need not equal the pushforward of each representative $N_\alpha$.

**(e) Universality.** Every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data
admits a data-fixing development embedding into $Q$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c).

items.title: A countable dense subset of the universal development by rational timelike exponential steps from a dense subset of the initial surface
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ and the
family of member maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q_\alpha\subseteq Q$ be as
in [[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (c)-(d), so that $Q$ is a
Hausdorff locally Euclidean smooth four-manifold with a smooth Lorentzian
metric $\bar g$, the sets $Q_\alpha$ are open and cover $Q$, and
$\bar j(\Sigma)\subseteq Q$ is the embedded initial surface. Then there is a
countable subset $D\subseteq Q$ with:

**(a)** $D\cap\bar j(\Sigma)$ is dense in $\bar j(\Sigma)$; and

**(b)** $D$ is dense in $Q$.

Moreover $D$ can be chosen of the following explicit form: with
$D_0:=S_0$ a countable dense subset of $\bar j(\Sigma)$, and having chosen
once at its first occurrence for every $x\in D_n$ a basis $(e_1(x),\dots,e_4(x))$ of $T_xQ$ and defined
$$V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}:=\Bigl\{\sum_{i=1}^4q_ie_i(x):\ q_i\in\mathbb Q\Bigr\},$$
one sets
$$D_{n+1}:=D_n\cup\bigl\{\exp_x(v):\ x\in D_n,\ v\in V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}\text{ timelike, with }\exp_x(v)\text{ defined}\bigr\},\qquad D:=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}D_n.$$

items.title: Second countability of the universal development quotient from a countable dense set and exponential charts
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ and the member maps
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q_\alpha\subseteq Q$ be as in
[[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (c)-(d): $Q$ is a Hausdorff locally
Euclidean smooth four-manifold with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, the
open sets $Q_\alpha$ cover $Q$, and each $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$
is a diffeomorphism onto $Q_\alpha$. Let $D\subseteq Q$ be a countable dense
subset, as supplied by [[lem-gr-development-quotient-dense-set]]. Then $Q$ is
second countable ([[def-second-countable-space]]).

More precisely, choose one basis at each $d\in D$. In these coordinates let
$B_d(a,r)\subseteq T_dQ$ be the Euclidean open ball centered at
$a\in\mathbb Q^4$ with radius $r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}$, and let
$\mathcal E_d$ be the maximal exponential domain. Then
$$\mathcal B:=\{\exp_d(B_d(a,r)):d\in D, a\in\mathbb Q^4, r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}, B_d(a,r)\subseteq\mathcal E_d, \exp_d|_{B_d(a,r)}\text{ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of }Q\}$$
is a countable basis of the topology of $Q$.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the smooth maximal globally hyperbolic development of constrained initial data in the selected matter sectors
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$,
$\kappa>0$, let $\Sigma$ be a connected smooth three-manifold with smooth
Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric $2$-tensor $K$, and let smooth
complete matter initial data be given for one fixed admissible covariant coupled model of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]], with the constraints satisfied and at least one development existing. The supplied local existence and uniqueness obligations must hold for that same model and for the complete data at every spacelike restart used in the proof. This includes vacuum, scalar, strict barotropic fluid and geodesic nonnegative tilted dust (with velocity prescribed through zero density) via [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]]; additional fixed models must supply the same actual obligations. Then there exists a development
$(M_{\mathrm{max}},g_{\mathrm{max}},N_{\mathrm{max}},j_{\mathrm{max}},\psi_{\mathrm{max}})$
of the data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]
clause (a) that is maximal in the sense of clause (d) of that definition:
for every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data there is a
data-fixing development embedding $M\to M_{\mathrm{max}}$. Moreover, if
$(M'_{\mathrm{max}},g'_{\mathrm{max}},N'_{\mathrm{max}},j'_{\mathrm{max}},\psi'_{\mathrm{max}})$
is another maximal development of the same data, then there is exactly one
data-fixing isometry $M_{\mathrm{max}}\to M'_{\mathrm{max}}$; the maximal
development is thus unique up to a unique data-fixing isometry. It is
connected and, by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]],
globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface $j_{\mathrm{max}}(\Sigma)$.

items.title: Conditional model deduction: the adopted field law and matter model yield a maximal globally hyperbolic development of constraint-satisfying initial data
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the mathematical suppliers.

Adopt the postulates [[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] (the Einstein field law
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ for a Lorentzian four-metric $g$ with
cosmological constant $\Lambda$ and coupling $\kappa$),
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] (the classical smooth Lorentzian
domain, time orientation and the identification of $g$ as the gravitational
field), and [[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] (the selected matter
sectors, their equations of motion and stress-energy tensors, and the
requirement that the coupled system be treated within the stated
regularity).

Adopt the specified fixed matter equations and stress expression as model premises as well; for any additional model beyond the concrete sectors of the cited postulate, these are additional stipulated premises. Mathematical admissibility does not itself assert a physical matter law.

Let $\Sigma$ be a connected smooth three-manifold, let $h$ be a smooth
Riemannian metric and $K$ a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor on $\Sigma$, and let
complete smooth initial data for one fixed admissible coupled model of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] be given, satisfying the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]. Assume its actual local existence and uniqueness/restart hypotheses, including complete matter initialization and recovery. The concrete branches of [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] include vacuum, scalar, strict fluid and nonnegative tilted geodesic dust with velocity through zero density; any further model must supply the same fixed-model obligations. Then, as a conditional deduction from the
adopted model:

**(a)** there exists a development
$(M_{\mathrm{max}},g_{\mathrm{max}},N_{\mathrm{max}},j_{\mathrm{max}},\psi_{\mathrm{max}})$
of these data in which $g_{\mathrm{max}}$ solves the adopted field law with
the adopted stress-energy tensor and the matter fields solve the adopted
matter equations, and which is maximal among developments of the same data
in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (d);

**(b)** every development of the same data admits a data-fixing development
embedding into $M_{\mathrm{max}}$, and any two maximal developments of the
same data are related by exactly one data-fixing isometry; thus within the
model the maximal development is determined by the initial data up to
isometry fixing the initial surface;

**(c)** $M_{\mathrm{max}}$ is globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface
$j_{\mathrm{max}}(\Sigma)$, so the deduction yields a deterministic
initial-value formulation inside the model for those complete constrained data that also satisfy the stated admissibility and local/restart hypotheses.

The conclusion is a statement about the adopted model: it asserts that the
postulated equations, together with the mathematical hypotheses on the data
and the regularity requirements of the sector, imply the existence and
uniqueness of the maximal development as a conditional consequence. It makes
no assertion that the model or its data describe any observed system, and
carries no empirical content beyond the model premises.

items.title: Scope and empirical qualifications of the maximal globally hyperbolic development: model content, idealisations, and no observational claims
items.statement:
This remark records how [[pthm-gr-smooth-maximal-development]] is to be
read; it adds no new mathematical claim.

**(a) The deduction is conditional on the adopted postulates.** The
existence and uniqueness of the maximal development is a logical consequence
of [[post-gr-einstein-field-law]],
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]],
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] and the mathematical theorem
[[thm-gr-smooth-maximal-globally-hyperbolic-development]], applied to data
that satisfy the constraints, complete-data regularity and actual local existence/geometric uniqueness/restart hypotheses of the fixed admissible coupled model in [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]. Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are mathematical premises. The vacuum, scalar, strict-fluid and nonnegative tilted geodesic dust branches of [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] are included, with independently prescribed dust velocity through zero density; the conclusion is not confined to those four models and does not follow from an arbitrary conserved stress tensor.
Granting the postulates, the deduction is a theorem about the model; it is
not evidence that the model describes nature.

**(b) The initial data are model inputs, not observations.** The data
$(h,K,\psi_0)$ are idealised smooth fields on an idealised smooth connected
three-manifold; constraint-satisfying choices are mathematical objects. If a
physical situation is modelled by such data, the accuracy of that modelling
and the errors in choosing the data are separate questions not addressed by
the deduction. No measurement, apparatus, sample or statistical inference
occurs in the delivered claims, and none should be attributed to them.

**(c) Maximality is a statement inside the smooth globally hyperbolic
class.** "Maximal" in [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause
(d) means: every smooth development of the same data embeds into
$M_{\mathrm{max}}$ by a data-fixing development embedding. It does not mean
that $M_{\mathrm{max}}$ is geodesically complete, that no larger Lorentzian
manifold of any kind extends it, or that it maximises any geometric
quantity. Extensions that are not globally hyperbolic, or
$C^k$-developments with $k<4$ in the sense of the sector's regularity, are
outside the class compared by the theorem.

**(d) Uniqueness is up to a unique data-fixing isometry.** Two maximal
developments of the same data are isometric by exactly one isometry
commuting with the initial embeddings and preserving the matter fields and
time orientation; the "solution" of the model's initial-value problem is an
isometry class of developments, not a distinguished coordinate
representative. The uniqueness conclusion says nothing about the
multiplicity of stationary or periodic solutions of the field equations
unrelated to the given data.

**(e) Regularity, matter and topological hypotheses are active.** The
deduction requires the smooth four-dimensional regularity of the adopted
domain, the fixed covariant coupled matter model with its full equations and stress expression, the smoothness and completeness of the initial data
in the sense of the constraint framework, and the second countability of the
initial manifold. If the sector assumptions are modified (for example to
non-smooth matter, matter with additional gauge freedom, or a different
stress-energy model), the deduction must be re-established for the modified
system; the mathematical reductions of
[[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] are exactly where
those hypotheses enter.

**(f) No claim about the observed universe.** The statement that "given
initial data, the model has a maximal development" is a conditional
deduction. It does not assert that the actual universe is globally
hyperbolic, that smooth initial data describe any particular epoch, or that
any observed phenomenon is predicted by the development of specific data.
Comparisons of developments with observations test the combined model and
apparatus assumptions; agreement is evidence and not a proof of the model.

items.title: The maximal development of the flat vacuum data is Minkowski spacetime
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the invoked general causal and maximal-development suppliers.

Take $\Sigma:=\mathbb R^3$, $h$ the Euclidean metric $\delta$, $K:=0$,
$\Lambda:=0$, $\kappa>0$ and the vacuum sector of
[[thm-gr-smooth-maximal-globally-hyperbolic-development]] (no matter fields,
$T=0$); the constraint equations reduce to $0=0$ and are satisfied. Then
the maximal development of these data is, up to a unique data-fixing
isometry, four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime
$(\mathbb R^4,\eta)=(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta)$ with the standard initial
embedding $j:\Sigma\to\mathbb R^{1,3}$, $j(x)=(0,x)$, and time orientation
$N=\partial_t$.

references.title: J. Sbierski, On the Existence of a Maximal Cauchy Development for the Einstein Equations - a Dezornification, arXiv:1309.7591v3 (2015): Theorem 2.8, whose flat vacuum instance is the example discussed here, printed pp. 12 and 20-24

items.title: Maximal common development and gluing of the flat vacuum data with its translate
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the invoked general causal and maximal-development suppliers.

Let the flat vacuum data of [[ex-gr-minkowski-maximal-development]] be given
($\Sigma=\mathbb R^3$, $h=\delta$, $K=0$, $\Lambda=0$, vacuum). Let
$M:=(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta)$ with the embedding $j(x):=(0,x)$ and let
$M':=(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta)$ with the translated embedding
$j'(x):=(1,x)$; both are developments of the same data (in $M'$ the slice
$\{t=1\}$ has induced metric $\delta$ and vanishing second fundamental form
and is a Cauchy surface). Let $\psi:M\to M'$ be the time translation
$\psi(t,x):=(t+1,x)$. Then:

**(a)** $(M,\psi)$ is a common subdevelopment of $M$ and $M'$, and it is the
maximal common development;

**(b)** the glued quotient of [[lem-gr-development-pair-gluing]] is
isometric, in a data-fixing way, to Minkowski spacetime itself, the two
embeddings being the identity and the inverse translation.

references.title: J. Sbierski, On the Existence of a Maximal Cauchy Development for the Einstein Equations - a Dezornification, arXiv:1309.7591v3 (2015): Theorem 2.7, whose simplest non-identical instance is the example discussed here, printed pp. 20-22

items.title: The spacelike restart level set of the time separation from a point in Minkowski spacetime
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the invoked general causal and maximal-development suppliers.

In Minkowski spacetime $(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta)$ with metric
$\eta=-dt^2+dx^2$ and time orientation $\partial_t$, let $q:=(1,0,0,0)$ and
$0<\tau_0<1$. The time separation from $q$
([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]]) is
$$\tau_q(r)=\sqrt{(t-1)^2-|x|^2}\qquad\text{for }r=(t,x)\in J^-(q),$$
and equals $0$ otherwise. Then the level set
$$S:=\{r\in I^-(q):\tau_q(r)=\tau_0\}$$
is a smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface, every causal curve meets it in
at most one parameter value, and every point of $S$ is the past endpoint of
a future-directed timelike geodesic segment of length $\tau_0$ ending at $q$, namely the radial
segment $s\mapsto r+\frac{s}{\tau_0}(q-r)$ for $s\in[0,\tau_0]$, where
$r=(1-\sqrt{\tau_0^2+|x_s|^2},x_s)$.

references.title: J. Sbierski, On the Existence of a Maximal Cauchy Development for the Einstein Equations - a Dezornification, arXiv:1309.7591v3 (2015): the level surface S = tau_q^{-1}(tau_0) cap W cap I^+(iota(M)) and formula (3.12) in the proof of Theorem 3.6, printed p. 19
R. M. Wald, General Relativity, University of Chicago Press 1984: the Lorentzian distance function and its level sets in Minkowski spacetime, Chapter 9

items.title: The rational timelike exponential set and the rational exponential basis in the flat vacuum development
items.statement:
In the flat vacuum development $M=(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta)$ of
[[ex-gr-minkowski-maximal-development]] with initial embedding
$j(x)=(0,x)$, take $S_0:=\mathbb Q^3\subseteq j(\Sigma)$ and the standard
coordinate basis at each point. Then the recursion of
[[lem-gr-development-quotient-dense-set]] produces the countable set
$$D=\mathbb Q\times\mathbb Q^3=\mathbb Q^4,$$
which is dense in $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ and meets the initial surface in the
dense set $\mathbb Q^3\times\{0\}$; and the associated exponential family
$$\mathcal B=\Bigl\{d+B(0;r):\ d\in\mathbb Q^4,\ r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\Bigr\}$$
(the Euclidean balls with rational centre and rational radius, because
$\exp_d$ in Minkowski spacetime is $v\mapsto d+v$ in the standard
coordinates) is the standard countable basis of the topology of
$\mathbb R^4$, so $M$ is second countable.
